title: Tunisia's installed wind capacity was 245 MW at end-2024, below the 2015 plan's 775 MW target for 2020

rootCauses.cause: Before the 2015 renewable-electricity framework, private generation was constrained to state-tendered concessions and unsolicited projects were not allowed; IRENA reports that only one concession agreement, for a 471 MW independent power producer (Carthage Power Company), had been granted. This helps explain why the initial wind fleet was developed by STEG, but does not by itself establish why no additional wind capacity appears in the cited end-2024 series.

IRENA reports that offers in the May 2017 wind authorisation call depended on PPA changes and that no wind project was selected in that call. It describes a subsequent revised-contract process and later separate concession tenders. The evidence documents project-development barriers and delays but does not establish that Law 2015-12 alone caused the capacity gap.

A 2019 tier-C press report said 17 of 143 Metline-Kchabta turbines were fully stopped since 2015 and attributed this to theft/vandalism, delayed replacement and maintenance issues; a STEG official cited slow purchasing and spare-part import procedures. These are reported explanations, not independently verified fleet-wide causes of the output trend.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.content:
Tunisia's current wind-generation fleet was developed by STEG in two main build-outs: Sidi Daoud began operating in 2001 and reached 55 MW in 2008; Metline and Kchabta in Bizerte entered in 2012 with 190 MW combined (SRC-TG-106). The 2015 Tunisian Solar Plan recorded 245 MW installed wind capacity at its baseline and planned 775 MW by 2020, 1,305 MW by 2025 and 1,755 MW by 2030 (SRC-TG-192). IRENA's energy profile reports 245 MW at end-2024 and zero net wind-capacity change over 2019-2024 (SRC-TG-190). Thus the documented national capacity remained at 245 MW at the 2015 and 2024 endpoints, and it was below the plan's 2020 and 2025 planned totals; these planned values are targets, not forecasts or evidence of actual capacity. The available sources do not establish exactly when the plateau began or why additional wind capacity was not commissioned.

Wind electricity generation also declined over the reported series: IRENA gives 507 GWh in the 2014 peak year and 449 GWh in 2017 (SRC-TG-106); ONEM reports 500 GWh in 2019 and 465 GWh in 2020 (SRC-TG-194), then 337 GWh in 2024 and 259 GWh in 2025 (SRC-TG-193). ONEM labels the 2024-2025 change as -23%; it reports wind as 1.3% of the 2025 electricity-production mix, whose total includes self-produced PV (SRC-TG-193). These are generation data, distinct from installed-capacity values. The evidence establishes the output trend but not its cause.

sections.heading: Root causes and explanations
sections.content:
The available sources identify historical policy and project-development constraints, but do not prove a single root cause for the capacity plateau or output decline.

- **Historical public-utility-led build-out.** IRENA reports that before the 2015 framework private generation was limited to concessions tendered by the state, unsolicited private power production was not allowed, and only one concession agreement had been granted, for a 471 MW independent power producer (Carthage Power Company). The existing wind farms were developed by STEG (SRC-TG-106). This explains the institutional context of the original fleet; it does not establish that the pre-2015 framework alone caused the later lack of capacity additions. The 2015 Solar Plan still assigned STEG 545 MW of wind capacity by 2020, compared with a 245 MW 2015 baseline, but IRENA's end-2024 data show 245 MW in total (SRC-TG-192, SRC-TG-190).
- **Documented procurement and project-development constraints.** IRENA says most offers in the May 2017 authorisation call were conditional on changes to the standard power-purchase agreement; it reports that no wind project was selected in that call and describes revision of the contract (SRC-TG-106). The May 2017 call's wind proposals were deferred pending PPA revision; under the separate authorisation process, four wind authorisations were granted in January 2019. The 2018 concession prequalification was a different process and covered four wind farms totalling 500 MW (SRC-TG-106). FNF's ministry-assisted 2023 policy paper says a deadline for 300 MW of concession wind projects extended to end-2023 to allow studies and wind-speed measurement; ONEM's 2025 report separately says a state-site wind measurement campaign was due to start in early 2026 and lists one awarded 75 MW private-site wind project under the 2022 tender (SRC-TG-195, SRC-TG-193, p. 41). ONEM's later September 2026 bulletin dates the same campaign to early 2027 and the 75 MW award to January 2026 (SRC-TG-100, p. 39). Those dated statements document delays and development activity, not the late-2026 status of each project or proof that one law caused the gap. FNF also reports that defence coordination is required for wind projects because of strict siting criteria (SRC-TG-195).
- **Reported turbine outages.** A 2019 WMC/TAP report said 17 of 143 Metline-Kchabta turbines were fully stopped since 2015. The article attributed damage to theft and vandalism and delayed repairs to lack of maintenance, replacement parts, slow purchasing and import procedures; these are press-reported claims, including statements attributed to TAP documents and a STEG official (SRC-TG-197). They support a dated, site-specific report of outages, not a verified explanation for national generation changes through 2025.
- **El Haouaria rehabilitation report.** La Presse reported in September 2026 that the Sidi Daoud/Borj Essalhi plant was being rehabilitated, with 32 old turbines to be replaced by seven new turbines; it reported a 102 million dinar loan-funded project and completion expected in 2027 (SRC-TG-198). The same article gives current production capacity as 10.5 MW and a future range of 29-33 MW, but does not define the measurement basis for either. These press figures are retained as reported project details and are not treated as official installed capacity or as a confirmed cause of the national generation decline.

sections.heading: Evidence and interpretation
sections.content:
- **Observed capacity:** 245 MW at the 2015 baseline in the Solar Plan; 245 MW at end-2024 in IRENA; IRENA reports zero wind-capacity change over 2019-2024 (SRC-TG-192, SRC-TG-190). This supports endpoint continuity and the 2019-2024 flat series, not an exact start date for stagnation.
- **Plan targets:** the 2015 plan's planned totals were 245 / 775 / 1,305 / 1,755 MW for 2015 / 2020 / 2025 / 2030; planned STEG wind capacity was 245 / 545 / 645 / 735 MW at those horizons (SRC-TG-192, p.15). The 2020 and 2025 values are planned capacity, not achieved outcomes. The same plan distinguishes a 35% renewable share of installed capacity from a 30% renewables share of electricity production by 2030; these are different measures (SRC-TG-192).
- **Generation:** reported STEG wind generation was 507 GWh (2014), 449 GWh (2017), 500 GWh (2019), 465 GWh (2020), 337 GWh (2024) and 259 GWh (2025), from IRENA and ONEM (SRC-TG-106, SRC-TG-194, SRC-TG-193). IRENA separately lists 338 GWh for 2023 (SRC-TG-190). The series is not a continuous annual series in this record, and the cited reports use different publication years and presentations. ONEM's 2025 table identifies its production values as GWh and labels the year-over-year wind change -23%; the accompanying mix chart says it includes self-produced PV in the total denominator (SRC-TG-193).
- A simple arithmetic comparison of 259 GWh in 2025 with 245 MW nameplate capacity implies about 12% annual energy per nameplate capacity (259,000 MWh / (245 MW x 8,760 hours)). This is an indicative calculation across sources and is not a reported capacity factor or verified availability measure; the 2014 output similarly implies about 24% if divided by 245 MW (SRC-TG-193, SRC-TG-190, SRC-TG-106).

sections.heading: Confidence and timeframe
sections.content: Capacity and generation figures are reported by IRENA, ONEM and the official 2015 Solar Plan; the cited 245 MW capacity value recurs across the plan baseline and IRENA's end-2024 series. Medium confidence reflects that the measured shortfall is clear but causal attribution for the plateau and output decline remains unresolved; the outage and rehabilitation detail is press-reported (tier C). `current` is used because the documented national capacity endpoint and generation series run through 2025, while the historical build-out and policy context are retained to explain the issue.

sections.heading: Links to other sectors
sections.content: No direct cross-sector mechanism is established in these sources. Lower wind generation could increase reliance on other sources in the electricity mix, but the record does not establish that wind generation was replaced one-for-one by gas. FND-TG-101 discusses the separate gas-dominated electricity system.

sections.heading: Verification status
sections.content:
IRENA and the dated Solar Plan establish the capacity comparison. The separately sourced generation series measures electricity produced. Causes of the change in output and the size of any future rehabilitation are left open.

**Independent review, 21 November 2026:** pass after corrections. Originals checked: Tunisian Solar Plan 2015 (SRC-TG-192), p. 10 and p. 15 Figure 9 (245 MW baseline; 775, 1,305 and 1,755 MW; STEG 245, 545, 645, 735 MW); IRENA energy profile (SRC-TG-190), p. 2 capacity table and p. 3 generation; IRENA RRA Tunisia 2021 (SRC-TG-106), Sidi Daoud and wind generation text, Law 96-27 passage, May 2017 call and January 2019 authorisations; ONEM Chiffres cles 2020 (SRC-TG-194) and 2025 (SRC-TG-193), wind production rows, mix chart and p. 41 wind project table; ONEM Conjoncture energetique, September 2026 (SRC-TG-100), p. 39; WMC/TAP, 10 April 2019 (SRC-TG-197); La Presse, 29 September 2026 (SRC-TG-198); FNF policy paper 2023 (SRC-TG-195), Arabic text. Corrections made: the sole concession is described as a 471 MW independent power producer rather than "a gas plant", which the IRENA sentence does not say; the later September 2026 ONEM bulletin (SRC-TG-100), which moves the wind measurement campaign to early 2027 and dates the 75 MW award to January 2026, is now recorded alongside the 2025 report's "early 2026"; SRC-TG-100 added to sources. The reviewer's objection that the early-2026 campaign date and the 75 MW award are not in SRC-TG-193 was not confirmed: both are in the p. 41 table of the Chiffres cles 2025 PDF (an image table missing from the text transcript the reviewer used). The Sidi Daoud 2001 start year and 55 MW by 2008 were confirmed in SRC-TG-106. Independent teammate sign-off is outstanding; reviewer and author share the TahaGHZ identity, so the record is not validated.

p. 5, foreword:

> [...] with a 30/30 target to reduce primary energy demand by 30% in 2030 compared to the trend scenario; and renewable energy to 30% of the electricity production by 2030, in comparison to the installed 373 MW renewable energy in 2019.

English gloss: the "30/30" target is a 30% cut in primary energy demand against trend and 30%
renewables in electricity production by 2030. Installed renewables were 373 MW in 2019.

p. 23, 2.2:

> The monopoly on electricity generation, transmission and distribution from 1962 to 1996 was held by the Tunisian Company of Electricity and Gas (STEG – Société Tunisienne d'Electricité et du Gaz).

> Law No. 96-27 (April 1996) authorises the private generation of electricity through concessions provided by state authorities. It does not allow, however, unsolicited private power production (either from conventional or renewable sources). Only one concession agreement has been granted, authorising the creation and operation of Tunisia's first IPP (Carthage Power Company in Radès, 471 megawatts (MW)). This power station began operation in 2002 under a 20-year power purchase agreement (PPA).

English gloss: STEG held the generation, transmission and distribution monopoly from 1962 to 1996.
Law 96-27 (April 1996) allowed private generation by concession, but not unsolicited private
projects. Only one concession was granted, for the 471 MW Carthage Power Company plant at Radès,

PDF p. 9, strategy targets:

> وتم على ضوء هذه الاستراتيجية تحيين المخطط الشمسي التونسي الذي يهدف الى إدماج الطاقات المتجددة في المزيج الكهربائي بنسبة 35% في غضون سنة 2030 وتخفيض الاستهلاك بنسبة 30% في نفس الأفق.

English gloss: the Tunisian Solar Plan was updated to aim at 35% renewables in the electricity
mix by 2030 and a 30% cut in consumption by the same date.

PDF p. 13, self-production on medium voltage:

> تبعا الى هذه الإجراءات، تمّ إلى موفى سنة 2022 تركيز أكثر من 300 ترخيص بقدرة جملية في حدود 70 ميغاواط منها حوالي 30 ميغاواط تم ربطها بالشبكة.

English gloss: by the end of 2022 more than 300 self-production authorisations had been granted
for about 70 MW, of which about 30 MW were connected to the grid.

PDF p. 15, authorisation regime calls for projects:

> الدعوة الأولى لتقديم مشاريع (ماي 2017): تم إطلاقها في ماي 2017 لإنجاز 70 ميغاواط من الطاقة الشمسية الفولطاضوئية و140 ميغاواط من طاقة الرياح. [...] مع تأجيل مشاريع طاقة الرياح للدعوة الثانية بعد مراجعة العقد النموذجي
> الدعوة الثانية لتقديم مشاريع (ماي 2018): تم إطلاقها في ماي 2018 لإنجاز 70 ميغاواط من الطاقة الشمسية الفولطاضوئية و130 ميغاواط من طاقة الرياح. [...] و4 مشاريع طاقة رياح من فئة 30 ميغاواط
> الدعوة الثالثة لتقديم مشاريع (جويلية 2019): تم إطلاقها في جويلية 2019 لإنجاز 70 ميغاواط من الطاقة الشمسية الفولطاضوئية.
> الدعوة الرابعة لتقديم مشاريع (ديسمبر 2020): تم إطلاقها في ديسمبر 2020 لإنجاز 70 ميغاواط من الطاقة الشمسية.

English gloss: four calls for projects under the authorisation regime: May 2017 (70 MW PV and
140 MW wind; wind deferred to the second call after revising the standard contract), May 2018
(70 MW PV and 130 MW wind; four 30 MW wind projects among those granted agreements), July 2019
(70 MW PV) and December 2020 (70 MW PV).

PDF p. 18, concession regime, 2019 solar tender:

> إثر انقضاء الأجل النهائي لتقديم العروض في 19 جويلية 2019 بالنسبة لـ 500 ميغاواط طاقة شمسية فولطاضوئية، تلقت الوزارة 8 عروض مالية بأسعار منخفضة للغاية، كان أفضلها حوالي 72 مليما/كيلواط ساعة، أي ما يعادل 2,4 سنت-دولار/كيلواط ساعة. وفي 20 ديسمبر 2019، أعلنت الوزارة نتيجة طلب العروض، وتمت المصادقة على اتفاقيات المشاريع بموجب المراسيم أعداد 14 و15 و16 لسنة 2021 المؤرخة في 2021/12/14 وعدد 19 و20 لسنة 2021 المؤرخين في 2021/12/22.

English gloss: bids for the 500 MW solar concession tender closed on 19 July 2019; 8 financial
offers were received, the best at about 72 millimes/kWh (about 2.4 US cents). Results were
announced on 20 December 2019, and the project agreements were approved by decree-laws ("مراسيم") 14, 15 and 16
of 14 December 2021 and 19 and 20 of 22 December 2021.

PDF p. 18, wind concessions and 2022 tender:

> بالنسبة لمشاريع طاقة الرياح بقدرة 300 ميغاواط، تمتد آجال طلب العروض حتى نهاية سنة 2023 من أجل استكمال الدراسات الضرورية وحملات قيس سرعة الرياح.
> وخلال موفى سنة 2022، أصدرت الوزارة طلب عروض لإنجاز 1700 ميغاواط خلال الفترة 2022-2025 على النحو التالي: 800 ميغاواط من الطاقة الشمسية الفوطوضوئية على مواقع خاصة [...] 600 ميغاواط من طاقة الرياح على مواقع خاصة [...] 300 ميغاواط على موقعين مقترحين من الدولة (الهيشة قابس والخبنة سيدي بوزيد)

English gloss: for the 300 MW of wind concessions, the tender deadline was extended to the end of
2023 to finish studies and wind measurement campaigns. At the end of 2022 the ministry launched a
1,700 MW tender for 2022-2025: 800 MW PV and 600 MW wind on private sites, and 300 MW on two state
sites (El Hicha, Gabès and El Khobna, Sidi Bouzid).

PDF p. 18-19, section 3 "problems":

> رغم المجهودات الكبيرة التي بذلتها الوزارة المكلفة بالطاقة وهياكلها، إلا أن النتائج لم تكن وفق المأمول ويعود ذلك إلى العديد من الإشكاليات المتعلقة بالمسائل العقارية والتمويل والبيروقراطية وغيره.
> تواجه مشاريع إنتاج الكهرباء من الطاقات المتجددة صعوبات في الحصول على تراخيص في استغلال الأراضي الفلاحية المصنفة "مناطق صيانة" من قبل وزارة الفلاحة والموارد المائية والصيد البحري. لذلك قامت السلط العمومية بالعمل على تذليل هذه الصعوبات من خلال الأحكام التي تم تضمينها بالمرسوم عدد 68 لسنة 2022 المؤرخ في 19 أكتوبر 2022 [...] حيث تم بمقتضى الفصل 21 منه استثناء الأراضي المصنفة "مناطق صيانة" من التحجير بموجب قانون حماية الأراضي الفلاحية

English gloss: despite the ministry's efforts, results fell short because of land, financing,
bureaucracy and other problems. Projects struggle to get permission to use agricultural land
classified as "conservation zones" by the Ministry of Agriculture. Decree-law 68 of 19 October
2022 (art. 21) exempted such land from the ban under the agricultural land protection law, with
case-by-case review.

PDF p. 19, Ministry of Defence and wind:

> وتجدر الإشارة في هذا الصدد أن وزارة الدفاع الوطني تلعب دورا كبيرا في هذا المجال، خاصة فيما يتعلق بمشاريع طاقة الرياح. حيث تمتلك الوزارة معايير صارمة في خصوص هذا الصنف من المنشآت وهو ما يتطلب التنسيق المسبق.

English gloss: the Ministry of National Defence plays a large role, especially for wind
projects, with strict criteria that require prior coordination.

PDF p. 20, legal procedures, financing, grid, acceptance, regulation:

> تُعدّ مدة إنجاز الإجراءات المتعلقة بمشاريع الطاقات المتجددة طويلة حيث تستغرق مالا يقل عند ثلاث سنوات للانطلاق في الإنتاج
> تتطلب المشاريع المتعلقة بالطاقات المتجددة استثمارات ضخمة بحوالي 3 مليون دينار للميغاواط الواحد، في إطار تمويل مشروع (Project Finance) أي ان الضمان الأصلي للبنوك يرتكز على عقد بيع الكهرباء مع المشتري الوحيد والحصري وهو الشركة التونسية للكهرباء والغاز. وقد طلب العديد من المستثمرين رسالة طمأنة لتسهيل عملية التمويل.
> وقد تم اسناد رسائل طمأنة للمستثمرين في أوت 2022.
> وللإشارة لوحظ خلال الفترة الفارطة اقتراح بعض الدخلاء على القطاع لأسعار متدنية بغرض السمسرة أو لقلة الخبرة ثم تتعثر المشاريع بعد ذلك في الحصول على التمويل. ولحل هذا الاشكال تعمل الوزارة على إصلاح المنظومة المعتمدة فارطا من خلال ضبط التعريفة من قبل الوزارة ووضع معايير صارمة لقبول المشاريع للتأكد من جاهزيتها مسبقا (مصادقة البنك، الحصول على التراخيص، حيازة الموقع، ضمان بنكي...) بالإضافة الى مراجعة العقد النموذجي حتى يصبح أكثر مقبولية حيال البنوك الممولة.
> تعتبر مسألة قدم شبكة نقل الكهرباء أحد أهم العراقيل التي تحول دون التسريع في نسق إنجاز مشاريع الطاقات المتجددة [...] كما أن طول إجراءات الربط تمثل عائقا
> تمثل مسألة مقبولية مشاريع الطاقات المتجددة أحد أبرز التحديات التي يواجهها الانتقال الطاقي، خاصة في ظل الازمة الاقتصادية التي تمر بها البلاد. لذا، فان سقف تطلعات المتساكنين في المناطق القريبة من أماكن إنجازها عالية جدا فيما يخص قدرتها التشغيلية. علاوة على ذلك، فإن مسألة الإشكاليات العقارية تعود في جزء منها الى عدم انخراط المجتمعات المحلية في مسار إعداد وتنفيذ سياسات الانتقال الطاقي.
> يعتبر إحداث هيئة تعديلية للكهرباء من اوكد مطالب المستثمرين لتوضيح المسائل المتعلقة بالأسعار ووضع حدّ لمسالة تداخل الأدوار، حيث تضطلع الشركة التونسية للكهرباء بدور هام في هذا المجال وهو مال لا يتماشى مع قواعد الحوكمة والشفافية والممارسات الحسنة المعمول بها في هذا المجال. وتجدر الإشارة الى أنه تم اعداد مشروع قانون لإحداث هيئة تعديلية وتم عرضه على الاستشارة العمومية وهو حاليا جاهز للنشر.

English gloss: procedures take at least three years before production starts. Projects need
about 3 million dinars per MW under project finance, where the banks' main security is the
power purchase contract with STEG as sole and exclusive buyer; many investors asked for a
comfort letter, and comfort letters were issued in August 2022. Some newcomers bid very low
prices for speculation or from inexperience, and their projects then failed to reach financing;
the ministry is reforming the system by setting tariffs itself and screening project readiness
(bank approval, permits, site, bank guarantee) and revising the standard contract. The ageing
transmission grid is one of the main obstacles, and long connection procedures are a barrier.
Social acceptance is a major challenge in the economic crisis: nearby residents expect many
jobs, and land problems partly stem from local communities not being involved in energy
transition policy. Investors' most urgent demand is an electricity regulator, to clarify prices
and end overlapping roles, since STEG's large role does not fit good governance and transparency
practice; a draft law creating a regulator went through public consultation and is ready.
resolvedSources.notes:
Policy paper by a German liberal political foundation, written with two ministry officials,
so it is close to the ministry's own account. It describes problems but gives few figures on
how many projects were delayed or by how long. Prices in millimes are converted by the author.
The 35% target here differs from the 30% in the 2015 Solar Plan text (SRC-TG-192) and the 2023
strategy synthesis (SRC-TG-103).

resolvedSources.title: Dix-sept éoliennes de la centrale de Metline-Kchabta en panne depuis 2015
resolvedSources.extracts:
Article dated 10 April 2019, body text:

> Dix-sept (17) des 143 éoliennes de la centrale éolienne de Metline-Kchabta mise en place en 2012 sont en panne et en état d'arrêt total depuis 2015, sans que la Société tunisienne de l'électricité et du gaz (STEG) n'intervienne pour les réparer.

> Aucun travail de maintenance n'a été effectué au niveau de ce parc éolien en situation de délabrement total.

> Selon des documents parvenues à l'agence TAP, la situation du parc éolien de Metline-Kchabta est due principalement à la récurrence des actes de vols et de vandalisme des équipements mis en place, à l'absence d'intervention immédiate pour remplacer les pièces endommagées ou volées, outre le manque enregistré en matière de voitures tout terrain pour accéder au parc.

> "9 éoliennes ont été vandalisées et d'autres nécessitent juste des pièces de rechange pour fonctionner", a-t-il souligné.

> "La STEG œuvre à réparer ces pannes le plutôt possible", selon lui, imputant le retard à la lenteur du processus et du système des achats et aussi aux procédures d'importation des pièces de rechange nécessaires.

English gloss: 17 of the 143 turbines of the Metline-Kchabta wind farm (built 2012) had been
fully stopped since 2015. TAP documents blamed repeated theft and vandalism, no immediate
replacement of damaged or stolen parts, and a lack of off-road vehicles. A STEG official said 9
turbines were vandalised and others only needed spare parts, and blamed slow purchasing and
spare-part import procedures.
resolvedSources.notes:
Press report based on agency TAP and a STEG official (the article names him in a part not
quoted here). Tier C: single press source, 2019 snapshot; no later official count of
unavailable turbines was found.

resolvedSources.title: Nabeul : 102 millions de dinars pour moderniser la centrale éolienne d'El Haouaria
resolvedSources.extracts:
Article dated 29 September 2026, body text:

> Le projet doit permettre d'augmenter la capacité de production de la centrale, actuellement de 10,5 mégawatts (MW), pour la porter entre 29 et 33 MW.

> Le coût global de la rénovation de la centrale est estimé à environ 102 millions de dinars, financés sous forme de prêt par la Banque allemande de développement.

> Les travaux, qui devraient s'étaler sur environ 20 mois, comprennent notamment le démantèlement de 32 anciennes éoliennes.

> Celles-ci seront remplacées par sept nouvelles turbines dotées d'équipements modernes et offrant un meilleur rendement.

> Dans une déclaration à Diwan FM, le député Mohamed Ben Saïd a indiqué que les travaux devraient être achevés en 2027.

English gloss: the El Haouaria (Sidi Daoud) wind plant currently has a production capacity of
10.5 MW, to be raised to 29-33 MW. The renovation costs about 102 million dinars, lent by the
German development bank. Over about 20 months, 32 old turbines will be dismantled and replaced
by seven new ones. A member of parliament said works should finish in 2027.
resolvedSources.notes:
Press report relaying a member of parliament on a radio station; tier C. "Actuellement de
10,5 MW" is not explained; Sidi Daoud's nameplate capacity is 54.5-55 MW (SRC-TG-106,
SRC-TG-195), so the figure presumably means usable capacity of the ageing turbines, but the
article does not say so.
